title: Build a catch-all path from validated segments
businessContext: Implement a deterministic application policy used around a Next.js request boundary. The Worker executes your policy function, not a Next.js server.
problemStatement: Implement solution(input). Input {segments} is missing or an array. Missing/empty returns /. If any segment is not a string matching letters, digits, underscore or hyphen, return null. Otherwise join with leading / and no trailing slash.
constraints: Return exactly the documented JSON value, including every field.
Do not mutate input. Inputs follow the shapes described in the task.
These tests do not establish RSC rendering, cache invalidation, distributed concurrency or server authorization.
candidateTasks: Implement the policy and trace every boundary case.
Explain where this function would run in a Next.js application and which checks remain server-side.
Answer the interview variation without changing the base contract.
hints: Optional catch-all parameters and required catch-all parameters have different absence behavior.
Trace the smallest empty, repeated or invalid case before adding branches.
alternativeApproaches: No. URL admission is separate from filesystem containment. Resolve against a fixed root, reject escapes and symlinks as appropriate, and authorize the resource before reading.
commonMistakes: Treating a passing model as proof of framework or distributed-system behavior.
Silently coercing values outside the explicitly allowed input policy.

verification: Run the same policy at its real request boundary and test forged/untrusted inputs separately.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
